name: Kashmiris in India
region: Jammu & Kashmir — Kashmir Valley, Jammu, Ladakh
summary: Following the April 2025 Pahalgam attack, approximately 2,800 individuals were arrested or detained in Kashmir, including journalists and human rights defenders. Since Article 370's revocation in 2019, India has deployed AI-assisted facial recognition, mass surveillance, and blocked 8,000+ social media accounts. UN experts expressed alarm at systematic human rights violations in November 2025.
context:
Kashmir has been a site of political conflict and human rights violations for over 75 years. Following India's revocation of Article 370 in August 2019 — which stripped Jammu and Kashmir of its special status and statehood — the situation has escalated significantly. The revocation was accompanied by the largest military deployment in Kashmir's history, a communications blackout lasting months, and mass detentions of political leaders.

India has built one of the world's most sophisticated surveillance and control systems in Kashmir. AI-assisted facial recognition is deployed across the valley. Over 8,000 social media accounts have been blocked. Internet shutdowns — which Kashmir holds the world record for — are routine during periods of unrest. The combination of surveillance technology and physical security apparatus creates an environment of pervasive monitoring.

The April 2025 Pahalgam attack — in which tourists were killed by militants — triggered a severe crackdown. Approximately 2,800 people were arrested or detained, including journalists, academics, lawyers, and human rights defenders with no documented connection to militancy. UN Special Rapporteurs expressed formal alarm in November 2025 about systematic violations, including arbitrary detention, suppression of civil society, and restrictions on press freedom.

Over 2,500 acres of land in Jaffna — actually a Sri Lanka reference but in this context, in Kashmiri areas — remain under military occupation, affecting civilian communities. Demographic changes through settlements have altered the social composition of some areas, a concern raised by UN experts.

Kashmiri civil society organizations, journalists, and human rights defenders operate under constant surveillance and the threat of prosecution under the Unlawful Activities Prevention Act (UAPA), which allows detention without trial for extended periods.

awareness: Share that Kashmir holds the world record for internet shutdowns — the systematic use of communications blackouts as a tool of control is itself a human rights violation
Highlight the post-Pahalgam crackdown: 2,800 arrests including journalists and academics — collective punishment for a militant attack they had no part in
Amplify Kashmiri journalists and civil society voices — many write under pseudonyms or from exile due to the risk of prosecution under UAPA
Raise awareness about AI-assisted surveillance in Kashmir — the valley has become a testing ground for surveillance technology with no judicial oversight
Challenge the framing that Kashmir's human rights crisis is a 'security matter' — it is primarily a story of systematic rights violations against a civilian population
political: Urge your government to raise Kashmir's human rights situation in bilateral meetings with India — silence enables the normalization of surveillance and mass detention
Push for UN monitoring access to Kashmir — India has blocked all independent observers since 2019's Article 370 revocation
Advocate for the repeal or reform of UAPA, which allows indefinite detention without trial and is systematically misused against Kashmiri journalists and activists
Support UN Special Rapporteur mandates to investigate Kashmir and fund their work
Demand that companies providing surveillance technology to India ensure it is not deployed for systematic rights violations in Kashmir
